topic: 经济选择与完整议论文
grammarFocus: 复合句与简单句搭配；条件、让步和原因表达；标点。
title: The Repair Café and the Price of a Second Life
instructions: 阅读下面的文章（约650词），回答10个问题。文章为模拟教学材料，非真实新闻报道。问题类型包括单选、填空、匹配（用单选形式）和判断正误/未提及（三选一）。填空题答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。所有解释为中文，证据为原文引文。
passage:
A In the small town of Marlow, a group of volunteers opened a Repair Café last spring. The idea was simple: instead of throwing away broken toasters, lamps, and bicycles, residents could bring them to the community hall on Saturday mornings. Volunteers with tools and skills would try to fix them for free. The café was not a business. It was a response to a growing problem: the cost of replacing things was rising, and the amount of waste was rising too.

B The café’s first month was chaotic. Some people arrived with items that were clearly beyond repair. Others expected volunteers to work miracles in minutes. “We had to explain that we are not a magic shop,” says Lena Ortiz, one of the organisers. “If a part is missing, we cannot invent it. But if the problem is a loose wire or a worn belt, we can often help.” To manage expectations, the team introduced a simple rule: each visitor could bring one item per visit, and volunteers would spend up to thirty minutes on it. If the repair needed more time, the visitor could book a follow-up session.

C The rule changed behaviour. People began to think before they came. They checked whether a missing screw was really missing or just lost under the sofa. They watched online videos to see if a repair was possible. “At first, I was annoyed by the limit,” says Tomas Reed, a regular visitor. “But then I realised it made me more careful. I started to value the item more because I had to wait for my turn.”

D Not everyone was happy. Some residents argued that the café should charge a small fee. “If it is free, people will bring rubbish,” said one neighbour at a town meeting. “They will take advantage.” Lena disagreed. “We are not trying to compete with shops,” she explained. “We are trying to teach people that repair is an option. If we charge, some people who need help most will not come.” The meeting ended without a decision, but the café continued to operate on a donation basis. Visitors could put money in a box if they wished, but no one was required to pay.

E By autumn, the café had repaired over two hundred items. The volunteers kept records: 40 per cent of items were fixed on the spot, 35 per cent needed a follow-up, and 25 per cent could not be repaired at all. The last group was often the most instructive. “When we cannot fix something, we explain why,” says Ortiz. “We show the visitor the broken part. We tell them what a new part would cost. Sometimes the honest answer is that replacement is cheaper. That is also useful information.”

F The café has also changed the volunteers. Many of them are retired engineers or hobbyists. They say they enjoy the social side as much as the technical work. “I come for the coffee and the conversation,” says one volunteer. “The repairs are a bonus.” The café now runs a monthly workshop for young people who want to learn basic skills. The workshop is not free, but the fee is low, and it includes materials.

G Looking back, Ortiz is cautious about calling the café a success. “We have not solved the waste problem,” she says. “We have created a small space where people can ask questions. That is a start.” She believes the next step is to work with local schools. “If children learn that things can be repaired, they will carry that idea into adulthood. But we need teachers who are willing to try, and we need time. Neither is guaranteed.”

H For now, the café opens every Saturday from nine to twelve. The volunteers do not promise to fix everything. They promise to look, to explain, and to try. In a world where buying new is often easier, that promise is modest but real.

questions.prompt: What was the main purpose of opening the Repair Café?
options: To help residents repair broken items for free.
To sell second-hand goods at low prices.
To provide a place for retired engineers to meet.
To compete with local shops.
answers: To help residents repair broken items for free.
questions.explanation: 文章第一段明确说明志愿者免费修理居民带来的破损物品。
questions.evidence: Volunteers with tools and skills would try to fix them for free.

questions.prompt: According to paragraph B, what rule did the team introduce?
options: Each visitor could bring one item per visit and volunteers would spend up to thirty minutes on it.
Visitors had to pay a small fee before receiving help.
Volunteers would only repair items bought in the last year.
Visitors had to book a session at least one week in advance.
answers: Each visitor could bring one item per visit and volunteers would spend up to thirty minutes on it.
questions.explanation: 第二段提到团队引入规则：每人每次只能带一件物品，志愿者最多花三十分钟修理。
questions.evidence: each visitor could bring one item per visit, and volunteers would spend up to thirty minutes on it.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with ONE WORD from the passage: Some residents argued that the café should charge a small ______.
questions.explanation: 第四段中居民提出咖啡馆应收取小额费用，原文用词为 fee。
questions.evidence: Some residents argued that the café should charge a small fee.

questions.prompt: Which heading best summarises paragraph C?

The cost of replacement parts
A volunteer’s technical skills
The café’s opening hours
questions.explanation: 第三段主要讲述规则如何改变人们的行为，使人们更谨慎、更珍惜物品。
questions.evidence: The rule changed behaviour. People began to think before they came.

False
Not Given

options: True
False

questions.explanation: 第六段说许多志愿者是退休工程师或爱好者，并非全部都是退休工程师。

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The café has solved the town’s waste problem.
options: True
False
Not Given

options: 25 per cent
35 per cent
40 per cent

options: It depends on teachers’ willingness and available time.

grammar.title: 复合句与简单句搭配；条件、让步和原因表达；标点
grammar.explanation: 英语中，简单句只有一个主谓结构，复合句则包含两个或多个分句，常用连词连接。条件用 if 引导，让步用 although/though/even if 等，原因用 because/since/as 等。标点方面，复合句中从句在前时常用逗号隔开，如“If we charge, some people will not come.”；从句在后时通常不用逗号。
grammar.example: If we charge, some people who need help most will not come.

Although, it was raining they continued the repair.
answers: Although it was raining, they continued the repair.
questions.explanation: 让步状语从句在前时，主句前需加逗号；从句后不加逗号。
questions.evidence: Although it was raining, they continued the repair.

answers: Because the part was missing, we could not fix the lamp.
questions.explanation: 原因状语从句在前时，主句前加逗号；从句后不加逗号。
questions.evidence: Because the part was missing, we could not fix the lamp.
